A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, core models and propositions. All pages are readable, including v2 Appendices A-F; v1 ends after its references.

before.justification: V1 reports mathematical examples and proofs. Figure 1 illustrates analytic vector fields and energy contours, rather than reporting experimental, simulation-study or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: V2 retains Figure 1 and adds an explicitly schematic Figure 2. Its appendices provide model mappings and mathematical arguments, without original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Section 4 adds an illustrative gradient-flow model, u_dot = W^T g(Wu+b) - u, with energy ||u||^2/2 - L(Wu+b). The principal R(u)-based dynamics, three-energy construction and concrete choices in Examples 5-7 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or benchmark tasks. The retained activation-function examples and new theoretical boundedness discussion do not introduce training or evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains the same comparison between the Krotov-Hopfield energy and the proposed energy. The appendices discuss previously cited models but introduce no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: No experimental protocol is added or revised. Section 4 retains the same Figure 1 construction and choices of R and S; the new spectral restrictions are theoretical assumptions.

E4.justification: No ablation, robustness test, error analysis or empirical case study is added. Appendix C supplies a mathematical capacity argument, while Figure 2 is a conceptual illustration.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The expanded GOE and Tracy-Widom discussion concerns theoretical expectations, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 1 is visually identical, and no empirical scores, rankings or additional numerical evaluation results appear. The added capacity argument and eigenvalue formulas belong to the theoretical development.

T1.justification: New Appendix C derives a unique-memory result under rho(W)<1 and claims an extension to rho(W)=1. Appendix E expands the GOE derivation. V2 explicitly requires orthonormal V and nonsingular R, and Appendix F corrects bias and dynamics signs in Proposition 5's existing proof. The relocated proofs themselves were already present in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about dead neurons, Hessian-based stability analysis and alternative Lyapunov functions.

C2.justification: Section 2 and Appendix C add substantial discussion of boundedness, local stability and possible capacity loss from parameter restrictions. V2 also distinguishes compact from noncompact flat regions, qualifies sigmoid saturation through limits and floating-point arithmetic, and clarifies that preserving equilibria does not preserve attraction basins.

D1.justification: The Figure 1 generation description remains substantively unchanged. V2 supplies no new code or data access, numerical weights, solver settings, hardware or training details; its additional technical material consists of mathematical exposition.

R1.justification: The 33-item bibliography is unchanged. Section 2 refines attribution of the dense formulation to Krotov's Hierarchical associative memory [15]. Appendices A and D explain relationships to existing cited models, while Appendix C adds criticism of boundedness requirements in the cited literature.

P1.justification: Proof presentation is substantially reorganized: the inline proofs of Propositions 1, 3 and 5 move to Appendices B, E and F, alongside extended model-mapping explanations in A and D. New explanatory paragraphs and footnotes supplement the retained main section order. The main-text pointers to Appendices E and F are incorrectly swapped.

P2.justification: V2 adds the three-panel Figure 2 contrasting unbounded energy and compact versus noncompact flat regions. Figure 1 and the general visual style are retained; other changes principally involve equation presentation, caption references and pagination.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies assumptions and saturation, corrects proof signs and improves explanatory coverage. However, new Appendix C incorrectly extends uniqueness to rho(W)=1: its displayed equations with W=I and b=0 admit every nonnegative state as an equilibrium. Useful repairs to the existing reasoning therefore coexist with a substantive error in the main theoretical addition, leaving the net quality direction unclear.
